utterances.text: A transcript of what was said in the 2003 interview is before us for the purposes of this decision. In addition to the submissions we heard yesterday, both parties have been -- I think more accurately all parties, the Defence in combination, have been active overnight and have provided to the Chamber further brief submissions and authorities which we have found useful in our deliberations, and I thank counsel for their efforts in that regard. The issue is one necessarily arising only in an adversarial legal system. Not surprisingly, there is some apparent diversity in the present position between countries which have an adversarial legal procedure. To a large degree, this flows from statutory interventions. For example, the Criminal Procedural Act 1865 in the United Kingdom, and such from codification from the Federal Rules of Evidence applicable in the federal jurisdiction in the United States of America. Given this, in the Chamber's view, adequate appropriate guidance for dealing with this present application is to be found in the common law itself, which provides the foundation for the various adversarial legal systems. The general position is that a party calling a witness may not discredit that witness. Discredit is a complex concept of varying application, but this need not be separately developed for present purposes. Where a witness is unfavourable and also in the case of an adverse or hostile witness, the prohibition against discrediting is relaxed. There are, however, material distinctions between an unfavourable witness and an adverse one in this context. If the present application is to succeed on this dichotomy the witness must be shown to be adverse, or as it is often described, hostile. What, then, is an adverse or hostile witness? The statement in Stevens Digest of the Evidence, Article 147, has long been regarded as offering reliable guidance and has received express judicial approval. It reads: "If a witness appears to the judge to be hostile to the party calling him, that is to say not desirous of telling the truth to the Court at the instance of the party calling him." In that situation, the law has been long settled at common law that a judge may, as a matter of discretion, permit the examination by the party calling the witness to be conducted in the manner of a cross-examination to the extent which the judge considers necessary for the purpose of doing justice. As the English Court of Appeal has emphasised in the R. v. Thompson, a 1976 decision, this discretion was an established feature of the common law before statutory intervention. For example, as was said in Clark v. Saffery (1824), Ryan and Moody's Reports 126, "If a witness in the box shows himself to be decidedly adverse, it is always in the discretion of the judge to allow a cross-examination." See also Bastin v. Carew in the same report. To assess whether the witness is adverse or hostile in this sense, the Court will have regard to the witness's demeanour, the terms of any inconsistent statement, and the circumstances in which it was made. There is no distinction in principle in this respect between a witness who gives evidence inconsistent with a witness statement, one who is reluctant to say anything, or one who professes to have forgotten what happened. They are each but illustrative of possible situations, as were the three situations identified by me in the particular context of a previous application. There are very many decided cases to these effects. I would refer only to the Crown against Honeyghan and Sayles, a 1999 English Court of Appeal decision; the people against Hannigan, a 1941 Irish decision; Wawanese Mutual Insurance Company v. Hanes, a 1961 decision of the Supreme Court of Canada; and McLellan v. Bowyer, a 1962 decision of the High Court Of Australia. Whatever way in which it may be manifested, the determinative consideration is whether it appears to the Chamber that the witness is not prepared to tell the truth at the instance of the party calling the witness. That is the basis upon which we approach the present application, as was the case for the previous application. There are in the Chamber's appreciation differences of demeanour and as to the circumstances of the previous statements which served to distinguish the present case from the previous application of this nature in this trial. utterances.text: That is a matter, obviously, which should be taken up by you with those responsible for the funding and the consequential provision. Unfortunately in this demarcation world, that is not a matter for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Guy-Smith is the resident expert on this matter among all the Defence lawyers. I won't take up the time of the Tribunal now with the issue, but it's -- it's acutely a problem today. That is clear, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. What we will do now is adjourn now until a quarter to four and encourage counsel in the interim to see whether on that whole page there is one or more reference to spring, one or more reference to June, one or more reference to July of 1998, and we will look forward with interest to what emerges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just have a few points to address to the Court. The first is that we checked again the translation, and drawing the Court's attention to page 9 of the Albanian, the second line from the top, the sixth word in the line is "pranvere." That word, according to Oxford Albanian/English dictionary is "spring." I am going to, in any event, move on. I've already moved on from that passage. I'm moving on to other passages. I think it would be useful if I gave a more clear explanation of the transcript, the English transcript that is before the Court, because it's a little bit confusing and I think I can clarify that in a way that I hope --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you move on, in what way is it proposed to inform the Chamber of the result of the interpretation undertaken by the interpreters here? Is that going to happen or is that not?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I don't know. That's not something --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Or has it simply been agreed?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I don't know. That's something that I didn't undertake. That's something that the Defence may have undertaken, to have that word checked or have the tape checked. But I think that where we agreed is I'm going to move on from that passage, so I certainly had a good-faith basis to ask -- put the questions to him. I think the witness, as I said, acknowledged that he said -- that "spring" was said but he explained that he may not have heard that, which is why I moved on to the next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: When we adjourned, there was to be an approach made, there didn't seem a reason to put that particularly on any counsel, to invite the interpreters present in the Albanian booth to look at page 9 to identify if the word "spring," "June," and "July," appeared and where. Is any counsel in a position to bring the Chamber up-to-date on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes, in this sense, that halfway through the break I had the opportunity to speak to one of -- I'm afraid I don't know her name, one of the interpreters, who indicated they were prepared to do this, and I said this was the agreement and that she then disappeared down a corridor to do that but it may not have been enough time. The proposition, in fact, she made herself was that the -- instead of looking at page 9 as it stands on paper, it would be better for her to listen to the -- to the tape itself for that passage, as it were, or passages that appear on page 9 to see what dates, months, and seasons are mentioned. She added, also, I just make it clear, that there can be a difficulty where the witness speaks Kosovar Albanian and the interpreter speaks Albanian Albanian, if I can put it that way. And she was going to investigate that. There's a dialect difference that she indicated. But I don't have any results of that, and so therefore we agreed that Mr. Whiting should continue, and I think his further examination is going to concentrate on excerpts of the tape being translated as the tape is shown to the witness, so that might circumvent this problem again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Mr. Mansfield, and I'm grateful if indeed some work is to be done by the interpreters to facilitate the resolution of this issue, and we look forward to the product of that work as soon as it can be completed. And we therefore, Mr. Whiting, need the witness back or were you going to tell us something now about the English version?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think it would be useful if I could do that, explain how this translation was prepared. Looking at the English version, the first thing that was done is a transcript was made of all the English that could be heard on the tape, so the questions in English and the responses as interpreted by the interpreter at the interview. And that appears in the normal type in the interview. That is the English that is spoken. What then happened is an interpreter listened to the interview and watched it, and where there was a difference between the English that was spoken and the Albanian that was either then said or was being interpreted from, that was indicated in the transcript. If there was no difference, then there was no change made. And if a change is indicated, it is in the italicised block type. And this is sometimes you will see the answer repeated. You will see the answer as given by the interpreter and then a revised answer that was actually given which is in the italics. Again, if there is no italics, it is translated word-for-word and the English that is in the normal type is accurate. And just to bring this point home, I would ask the Court to turn to page 21 of the transcript, just to make this absolutely clear. In the passage that we were talking about, OL the investigator says, "Yeah, still talk about spring of '98." That was translated word-for-word. So there's no italics because it was accurate. There was no need for a revision. However, if you turn now to page 23, about -- a little more than halfway down the page there is OL and it says: "O.L.: This was evident by June of 1998." Now here you see DB saying: "D.B.: And this was clear to you in June 1998? Meaning that the orders that came from command... and below... were implemented?" So in other words, in that instance it wasn't translated word-for-word; more was said in a slightly different way, and so that's why the revision is included in the italics. In preparing the tapes, the transcript for the tapes, I have asked them to rely on the italics where that is present so that we have the most accurate translation possible. So in other words, it has already been done that the Albanian that was said -- the Albanian questions by the interpreter and the Albanian responses by the witness have been checked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that, Mr. Whiting, and on the basis mooted between counsel, we should proceed and the witness may be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, for your patience. I hope we can continue now. Mr. Whiting still is questioning you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to ask you to turn again to page 9 of the Albanian transcript. Do you have that before you?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that we switch to Sanction, please. I'm going to play that last clip once again because we had the interruption. And, Witness, if you want to watch and following along in the transcript, you may.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: "O.L.: Like ... I ... what I'm trying to ask is ... is when some kind of ... a real organisation was able to be seen in the KLA? "R.B.: Yeah, was... was more visible in the... in June '98. "O.L.: Okay. "R.B.: As the numbers of... the number of soldiers increased. Yeah... They got some supplies... weapons supplies from Albania. So there were... there were some clashes with Serbian army in Carraleve. Yeah... I was ... I was wounded on the 17th of June, '98... after three hours of ... see, this was... this was... this was what I saw as an army of them forming and increasing in numbers and an army able to fight. "O.L.: Yeah. Do you ... do you have any idea of ... at this time who was the Supreme ... was there a Supreme Commander of the KLA in Kosovo? "R.B.: Yeah. As far as Pastrik zone is concerned, I... knew very well that Fatmir Limaj was the commander. And I knew as well that Shukri Buja and Ramiz Qeriqi was battalion commanders... I believe that people... people at the top would... take more care of organising better the army of ... of providing the proper structures... so we got also warnings or we got instructions... how to behave, what to do... to go by the book, to go by the UCK set of rules. "O.L.: Could you already during the first months, say the spring, summer of '98, was it possible for you to see that it worked as... an actual army? I'll explain this a little bit better if you first ... "D.B.: Aha ... "O.L.: Could you... experience that ... that the orders came from ... from the, say, Headquarters level, for example from Klecka to Shukri Buja and... then out to the soldiers? "R.B.: Yeah. I was... I was convinced the way it was, it worked. "O.L.: Okay "R.B.: And I've done my best in every case to comply by the rules... in order not to ... to contravene the rules "A.W.: And this was evident by June of 1998? "O.L.: Was it ... could you ... could you experience ... the power, for example, of say, Fatmir Limaj that he... he was the one giving the orders? Was that obvious in your ... in your work as a soldier? "R.B.: No... not as a name. I received orders from ... from Luan, from Ramiz. So I didn't know where he received his orders "O.L.: Okay. But ... but was it clear that the orders that you got from Ramiz Qeriqi, for example, was ... they were ... they were orders that had come from a higher level?"

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, were you able to watch? Were you able to follow that portion of the interview?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You would agree, would you not, that you said there that in -- by June of 1998, there was a headquarters in Klecka; right? That's what you said?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I gave the statement, about five years had passed since the war, and so I didn't concentrate so much on the time than I did on the year. And I think I told you yesterday that our battalion, Ruzhdi Selihu - it was called after the name of the martyr, the guy who laid down his life in July 1998 - I referred to him as a battalion, but before he was -- it was not a battalion. It was point Sokoli 1, Sokoli 2 point in Pjetershtice. So as I said I did not focus on the month than on the year. I gave several interviews. After your interview, I had to go into deeper details to explain some things which were not very clear to me then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Before we get to the explanation for your change in your testimony, my question is simple. Did you -- would you agree with me that you said in this interview that in June of 1998 there was a headquarters in Klecka? That is what you said in the interview; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it in the interview, but I concentrated more on 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you would agree with me, wouldn't you, that you were the one who came up with June, not the investigator? It was you who said June. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I might have said so, but it was wrong. The main thing being I concentrated on 1998 and not on the date and the month.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But, sir, actually in fact you were very specific about the dates and the timing because you said you fixed the date with the fighting in Carraleve which commenced on the 14th or the 17th of June. Isn't that right? So you were very specific about the date.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't very specific, but this is what I thought then. But regarding the -- the attack, that I knew the date in which it occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You've never forgotten the date of 17th of June, 1998, have you, because that was the date you were injured?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's a very clear date in your mind?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And so when you said in the interview that on the 17th of June that by the 17th of June of 1998 you understood that there was a headquarters in Klecka, that was something you remembered, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not that I knew for sure, but this is what I guessed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's -- in June of 1998, that's what you believed, that there was a headquarters in Klecka. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my personal belief, but as I said, I didn't focus on the month. I did focus on the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In June of 1998, you also believed that Fatmir Limaj was the commander of that headquarters in Klecka; is that right? That's what you believed in June of 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. After the formation of the brigades and battalions, it was then that I found out that Fatmir Limaj was the commander of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, in July or August, the battalions and brigades were formed, and it was all the 121st Brigade, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was called Brigade 121 Kumanova, because Kumanova was killed by the end of August. So the brigade took the name after him, after he was killed, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And your battalion was called the Ruzhdi Selihu Battalion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you know Ruzhdi Selihu?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were friends together in the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And he was killed in the battles on the 25th and 26th of July, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in July, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: At the end of July. 25th, 26th of July.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 26th of July it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And where was that? Where was he killed?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was killed in Zborce during the fightings, during the offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When your battalion was formed, was the Ruzhdi Selihu battalion the first name it was given?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So it could not have been formed until August of 1998, because he wasn't killed until the end of July 1998. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you were interviewed for the first time by the OTP in the interview that we have been watching, you didn't forget that, did you?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This I cannot forget.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No. Of course, because you knew Ruzhdi Selihu, and you've never forgotten the day he died; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We cannot -- no one can forget that offensive in Zborce.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So you have never forgotten that your battalion was formed after that in August of 1998. That's a fact that you have never forgotten. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not forgotten it, but before finding this membership card, I wasn't sure about the accurate time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What was it on the membership card, and if you want it before you we can put it before you, but can you tell me what it is on the membership card that suddenly changed your testimony? It's Prosecution Exhibit 117. Would you like it placed in front of you?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you don't need to. I know what it contains.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could you tell me what it is -- what is on that membership card that made you suddenly change your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It sayings that our battalion called Ruzhdi Selihu, and the date when the membership card was issued. That was the first time for me to get a membership card on the level of a battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And that was on the 18th of August, 1998. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But you've just told us that you've always -- you've never forgotten that your battalion -- you've always known that that battalion was formed in 1998. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I can't tell you for sure when it was formed. But I know this card was issued to me on the 18th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But what is on the card that made you suddenly think that there was no command in Klecka and that Fatmir Limaj wasn't in command in Klecka in May, June, and July of 1998? Can you tell me that, please?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the statement I gave to you in April 2003, I remembered some things. I remembered some changes made to the statement I gave. I always referred to the year when I talked, not about the months, because -- because changes occurred every month.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to draw your attention back to the transcript, because we have a transcript of the interview. And I'm going to draw your attention back to the page 9 and 10 of your Albanian transcript. And if you want for us to play the tape again of this portion, we can. But do you see that on two occasions you do, in fact, mention the month June 1998 when you're saying that there was a headquarters in Klecka? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that it was written and it is here, but I am saying it was not true. I may have made a mistake. As I said, I did not concentrate on the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now -- what you're telling us now is that you think you made a mistake, that you weren't concentrating on the time in the interview?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I said earlier, I did not concentrate on the time but on the year, because as I said, five years had elapsed and many things may be forgotten. And during the translation, things may have happened. I mean, mistakes may have happened. But the most important thing for you to know is that what I'm saying today is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it a fact that you simply don't want to say here in the courtroom what is the truth, and that is that in June and July of 1998, there was a headquarters in Klecka?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. That there was a general headquarters in June or July, this I don't know. I don't think there was. After there was the formation of the brigades and battalions then I believe there was a headquarters in Klecka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I know what you're saying today. What I want to focus on is what you said the first time you were interviewed. Now I want to draw you to the passage where you say: "I knew about the Pastrik zone especially very well, that it was Fatmir Limaj for example. And so the commander was Ramiz Qeriqi and Shukri Buja." Now, there's no doubt that you're talking about June and July there, is there?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I have talked about June and July. Because I'm certain there was no General Staff until the first offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, you know that after -- after the end of July 1998, Shukri Buja was no longer even in the Pastrik zone. You know that, don't you? He went to the Nerodimlje zone.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So when you say in this interview, when you talk about the structure of Fatmir Limaj, Ramiz Qeriqi and Shukri Buja, you must be talking about a time before the end of July when Shukri Buja was in the Pastrik zone. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And so --

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I have said. Yes, I've expressed those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And that was true, wasn't it, that in June and July of 1998, you believed that Fatmir Limaj was a commander in Klecka and that that was the general command of the area? You believed that in June and July of 1998, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought so about Luan and Shukri Buja, that they were there. But regarding Fatmir Limaj, as far as I know, I never said that he was from the beginning in Klecka or the zone commander. Then it was not called zone, but when I talked with you I referred to it as a zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No, but you did say that in your interview on a number of occasions. We've already seen more than one. Now, I don't want you to tell us what you believe or what you want to believe here today. What I want you to tell us is what you believed in June and July of 1998. Whether you've changed your mind now or not, in June or July of 1998, you believed that Fatmir Limaj was a command near Klecka, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have very good knowledge, but I'm repeating it. I did not concentrate on the months, as I am supposed to do now. Five years had passed. Many things were forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm asking you to concentrate on what you believed in June and July of 1998, which is what you said in your interview in April of 2003. What you -- even if you've changed your view today, what you believed in June and July of 1998 was that there was a headquarters in Klecka and that Fatmir Limaj was the commander there. Isn't that what you believed in June and July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. I never thought that there was a general headquarters in June and July.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, you did think it in the interview in April 2003, because that's what you said. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I may have said it, but I did not concentrate on the time, on the month. More on the year I concentrated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if that's true, can you explain to me why it is you said yourself "June 1998" when you were talking about this headquarters in Klecka and Fatmir Limaj in command? If you weren't concentrating on the month, explain to me how it is that you said June 1998.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying it again. Maybe a mistake has occurred, because as I said, I concentrated on the year. I may apologise for the mistake that may have happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So now your testimony is that you made a mistake in the interview. Can you explain to me how it is that you made this mistake over and over again in the interview? Not just one time, but over and over again?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Honourable Judges, right from the outset I said that from 1998 to 2003, things may be forgotten and that I rather concentrated on what happened in 1998 without focusing on the month as I am required to do now, that is in June, July, or May, June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You also said in this interview that you -- it was -- you believed that orders came from above to Luan. Do you remember saying that in the interview?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my belief. Mainly I received orders from Luan, and I enforced them through other soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you believed that these orders came to Luan from above, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said that I don't know where from Luan got his orders. You can find it in the script.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You're right, you do say that, but you also say that you thought he got them from above. That's what you believed; right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying it again. It is written. I don't know where from Luan got his orders. The main thing for me -- the most important thing for me was to carry out his orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But it is also written that you thought he got them from a higher level. And if you want me to show you where that is in the transcript, I can.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't need to. I know. I know what I have said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And that's what you believed, isn't it, that the orders came from a higher level? You weren't sure from whom, but you thought they were from a higher level. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was my belief, my personal belief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to show you another clip, and that is -- it's on page 19 of your transcript, sir. And on our transcript, on the English transcript, it's page 46. Do you have page 19 in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if I could intervene again. I'm so sorry to do this. You carefully indicated yesterday that where belief was being sought, then we should know the basis of the belief, and that's what Mr. Whiting said he was going to examine. So I'd ask -- I don't mind in what order it's done, but if that's the basis for the questions, we'd like that examined, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Than you. That's helpful. I will do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, before we look at this next clip, I'm going to ask you another question about what you have testified about. You have testified that you -- it was your personal belief that Luan received orders from a higher level. My question now is: What was that belief based on?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believed based on the fact that as I was cooperating with Luan, I believed that there was someone else cooperating with Luan as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And people would talk about a -- there was talk about a headquarters in Klecka, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In June of 1998.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, what made you think -- what made you think that there was a higher level above Luan? Was it something you heard?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't hear anything, and I don't know anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, you do know things, and my question is: How did you know it? Why did you think that there was a higher level? What was it based on?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I might have mentioned "level," but it is true that I said everyone cooperated with everyone else. As I cooperated with Luan, I believed that Luan cooperated with someone else, with another friend of his.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, that's not what you said in your interview. What you said in your interview is that you got orders from Luan and that you believed he got orders from a higher level. That's what you believed, right, at the time?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My belief was that he was cooperating with someone else. Luan was cooperating with someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Cooperating and at times getting orders from somebody else; right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for orders, I cannot be accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: My question is: You believed that orders came from a higher level to Luan? That's my question. In June and July. That's what you believed. And you've already told us that's what you believed, that orders came from a higher level. You've told us that here today.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not determine the time when. However, after the formation of the brigades, I believed that that's the shape it took, that he took orders from somebody else. And until the formation of the brigades, the cooperation existed between the points.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to suggest that you're not answering my questions. My question is that you -- you have already testified here, just a few moments ago, that you believed that -- that you believed that in June and July of 1998, Luan got orders from a higher level. We can look at the transcript, but that's what it says in the transcript. That is what you said. My question now is: What was the basis for that belief? Why did you believe that? Was it something that you saw? Was it something that was told to you, or are you unable to tell us the basis for that belief?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was my belief that the way I received orders from Luan and the way my soldiers carried out orders from me, that's how the cooperation was between others.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And somebody above Luan is what you mean; right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say cooperation again here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Fine, cooperation. Cooperation with somebody above Luan in Klecka?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, as for Klecka, I know that it existed after the offensive. I knew that there was Klecka before the offensive, but I did not know it in capacity of a General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And before the offensive you knew that Fatmir Limaj was the commander in Klecka, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander of the point, not of the General Staff. That's what I thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And that was before the offensive. You thought he was the commander of the point in Klecka?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I think, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, turning to -- we're going to turn to another passage now, and it's -- again it's page 19 of your transcript. Do you have that open? And it's page 46. And if you'd just -- if you'd just look at from the top of the page, I believe that you are describing the fighting in Carraleve in -- around the 23rd of June of 1998. Do you see that? Do you see -- and if you need to turn to the page before you may, but do you see that's what you're talking about in the interview?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to draw your attention to about two-thirds down the page in the Albanian transcript where -- and -- where the interpreter asks you: "Again, was Shukri Buja the main commander in Kroimire at the time?" Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To which period of the year does it refer to? I can see the names here, but to what time does it refer to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think that will become clear. I'm going to ask that that portion of the tape be played, and you can look at it. And if we could switch to Sanction, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: "D.B.: Yes "O.L.: Yes, and Luan was also there "D.B.: Yes, Luan as well "O.L.: And you still think the main headquarters was in Klecka at this time? "D.B.: Yes, that's right. "O.L.: Had you -- had you at this point got any more information about an area division of the zones or..."

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, you see that you're talking here about the time period at the end of June when there's the fighting in Carraleve; right? You see that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you -- you said that -- you agreed that Shukri Buja was the main commander in Kroimire at that time and that the General Staff was still in Klecka at this time? And this is the end of June. You said Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that; right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say so, but that's a mistake, because to my knowledge the General Staff was formed after the formation of brigades and battalions, while Shukri Buja, he was in Kroimire until the offensive in July.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand that's what you want to say today. My question is: At the time of the interview, you believed that in fact the headquarters existed in Klecka in June of 1998. That's what you believed and that's what you said, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say so, but it's possible that it is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But at the time you said it you believed it to be true, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the year, yes. For 1998, but not for the month. I focused on the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But once again the month is said here, and it's clear what you're talking about because you're talking about the end of June 1998 when there was the fighting in Carraleve, and you've already told us that you remembered that time period very well because that's when you were injured. So you did focus on the month in this interview, and you believed when you said this that this was true, that in June 1998 the headquarters existed in Klecka.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I focused on the time when fighting took place, when I got injured. I'm sure about this period, but as for the General Staff, I'm not sure that the time was referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when did you come to this change of view? When did you change your mind about this? Because in the interview you say June of 1998 is when the General Staff -- the headquarters was in Klecka. When did you come to a different view?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I was equipped with the transcript, I checked certain things. It is a fact that I did speak clearly on a level of a year, not of a month. However, I do mention it here again, that five years had passed from the war and the time when this statement was taken and certain things were forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you do focus on the month in the interview, it's because that's what you remembered at the time, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the months when I had fightings and participated in combat, when I was injured. I cannot forget these months.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you can't forget that in June of 1998 when you were injured that there was a headquarters in Klecka, as you said more than once in your interview; right? That is what you believed at the time in June of 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, we called it headquarters in conversation with you. I could not call staff or headquarters even Petrastica comprising six soldiers. There was a point in Klecka as well, but at that time whether it was a headquarters or not, I don't know. To my knowledge it was a point. I went there when I had to see the doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: We'll get to that. Now, in this answer, you talk about Shukri Buja as the main commander in Kroimire, and at the same time, at some time when he was the main commander in Kroimire, there was a general staff in Klecka. That's what you say in this answer. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that I have said that. I'm not saying that I didn't, but again I'm -- want to be clear. I did not call it a headquarters on that time, on that month.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, my question now is not about the month. It's about the fact that Shukri Buja was a commander in Kroimire at the -- let's not worry about what time period there is at the moment. He's a commander in Kroimire at the same time that there is a headquarters in Klecka. That's what you -- you have a -- that's what you believed; right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe that. I say it again here. I did not focus on the time. A General Staff existed only after the offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But at the time of your interview, you believe that the general staff existed at some time when Shukri Buja was a commander in Kroimire. That's what you believed at the time of the interview. And again, if you need to look at what you said in the interview you may, but that's what you said and that's what you believed; right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I said that, but I did not focus on the time when Shukri Buja, it is a fact, that was commander of the battalion that was in our point in Kroimire until the offensive of Zborce [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to move on to another portion in the interview, and I'm going to ask if the usher would please put off the witness the -- I have a copy. It's U003-3748. No, not on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, you remember this map?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember -- do you remember yesterday you told us that this -- that you signed this and that you made the line in yellow during the interview with the OTP in April of 2003? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what you said yesterday was that this -- you believed that this -- that you made this -- this line to represent the area as it existed at the end of the war. That's what you told us yesterday, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did not mention the time when, but it is approximately just before the war ended, when I had a clearer knowledge, although I mentioned that this was an approximate line. This was my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, let's look at the interview. Let's look at the tape of this portion of the interview. It's on page 51 of the English, and it's on page 22 of the Albanian. And I'm going to submit -- I'm going to submit to you, and we'll see it in a moment, that when you drew this line in the interview, it was the area that fell under the command of Klecka in July of 1998. I'm going to draw your attention again to page 22 of the Albanian. It's about halfway down -- well, about a third of the way down on the page. Do you have that in front of you, page 22?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And just so you know where it begins, do you see that the question: "And Lapusnik was under -- in the same staff that you ..."? Do you see that question about Lapusnik, about a third of the way down the page? And you start talking about the Pastrik zone and what area it included. See the: "The Pastrik zone included some ways toward Malisheva, toward the Komorane road." Do you see that in the interview?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that we switch to Sanction, and I'm going to play this portion of the tape for you, and in it it's -- you will see yourself drawing the line and describing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: "D.B.: This is ... this has been what Pastrik zone would consist of, all this line "O.L.: Let's get another pen. If we could ask you to try to line the ... line the area that was ... was under the headquarters in Klecka. "R.B.: I'm not hundred per cent certain ... "O.L.: It's what your opinion is. And we're now talking about this time when you're fighting in July of '98. "D.B.: Yeah, it's an approximate version, of course "O.L.: Yes, okay "D.B.: It's not ... "O.L.: Is Malisevo part of ... or Malisheva...Is it outside or inside the... "D.B.: Yeah, yeah it's part of "O.L.: Okay, so Malisheva is here, approximately so... Yeah... okay..
