So let's circle the ones that are comparable with Kroimire. "D.B.: I'm talking about places where we carried out our daily activities, sleeping, eating "O.L.: No. What I would like you to do is to ... in this whole Pastrik area... to show me the other headquarters comparable with Kroimire. "D.B.: Okay. "O.L.: Klecka is the main one. "D.B.: So as I was -- spent most of my time, I didn't move from my place. I mostly moved to take this duty of observing Carraleve. "O.L.: Yes, this is... but just your knowledge about -- was there, for example, something in Lladrovci? "D.B.: I don't know "O.L.: What about -- did Lapusnik have a headquarter of its own? "D.B.: Yeah. I think -- I think so. I believe I'm not certain about it. "O.L.: Okay. "D.B.: Yeah. I've never been there so it was ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, do you see now that in fact when you drew that yellow line in the interview, the outline of the area, it was in July -- this was the area under the command of Klecka in July of 1998? That's what you drew in the interview, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not focus on the months of July. And again, I say that I focused on the time after the offensive. And as for the zone, I knew that it was part of our zone. In addition, I would like to underline here a change that has been made. It was -- it should state Likovc.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Rather than --

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nekovce. Nekovce.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you for that correction. It is noted. This is, by my count, the fourth instance that we have looked at in this interview where you stated in some form or another that in June or July of 1998 there was a headquarters in Klecka that had some control over this area. It's the fourth time. Is it still your testimony that you said this because you weren't focused on the month? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had my solemn declaration to tell the truth, and I did not focus on the month.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you explain for us, then, how it is that if you weren't focusing on the month that we've now seen four times when the month is made clear and you describe the headquarters being in Klecka? How did that happen if you weren't focusing on the month?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will again say that I spoke at the level of a year, that there were some changes. I did not focus on the months that you asked. So I did not concentrate on the months that were discussed in the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Isn't the -- didn't -- isn't the truth that you, at the time of the interview, whether you've changed your view now, but at the time of the interview you did in fact believe these things to be true in June and July of 1998 and that later you changed that view? Isn't that what happened?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I changed my views when I found facts, when I found the membership cards. In addition, I remembered the case when the Battalion Ruzhdi Salihu was formed, how the battalion was named after him after he died. So this is how I made some things clear to myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No. I understand -- I understand that you have changed your view and you've explained that it was because you saw this card. But isn't it a fact after you saw this card and you changed your view that you believed in June or July that there was a headquarters in Klecka? That's what you believed at the time of the interview, and you then changed your view. Isn't that what happened?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believed it was a staff, but I did not focus on the time when.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you tell us, then, what it is that changed, in your view, when you saw the card? What changed? What did you believe before you saw the card and what did you believe afterwards? What is it that changed?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot change anything. Time speaks for itself. As I said, it's been five years. Some things have been forgotten. I mentioned the membership cards. I mentioned it as a battalion, as I said before. Maybe I spoke of it as a battalion, although it wasn't a battalion at that time. We spoke of it as a zone although maybe there were no soldiers there, but we spoke of it as a zone, and we do the same thing today.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, you have said that time has passed and memory -- maybe you have forgotten some things. This interview that you participated in was in April of 2003, approximately five years after the event. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You would agree that your memory then was better than it is today, isn't it, seven years after the event?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I receive the transcript, it is true that I went into details to check whether there were mistakes, what the mistakes were, what the changes were, what things lacking were. So things like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when you came to this new view, when was that? When did you change your view? How long ago was that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I got the transcript, after I read it, after I saw my interview, after I found the membership card, after I consulted some documents, and that's when I changed my opinion. I remembered the event of the killing of Ruzhdi Selihu of Kumanova. So I considered all these facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And after you got the transcript did you see that, in fact, you had said more than you had realised you had said? Did you wish you had not said so much during the interview with the OTP?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. From the beginning, I said that there are some shortcomings in the transcript and that certain things that we discussed had not been discussed in details and that I was not focused on the time. I was focused on the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you reviewed the transcript, did you find one instance, one instance where you said, "I'm only talking about the year here and not I'm not talking about any particular month"? Did you find anywhere in the transcript where you made that clear?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There might be, but I'm not sure. I forget.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask you to go through the whole transcript now. I think you can take my word that that does not occur in the transcript. There is no place in the transcript where you say, I'm only talking about a year here. I can't focus on a -- I can't tell you anything about a particular month. If we can move to another part of the transcript. I'm going to ask you to look at page 29 of the Albanian, and it's page 80 of the English. I'm going to draw your attention to about halfway down the page of 29 in the Albanian. And do you see that --

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm just going to ask you if you could look at -- read over the second half of page 29 and the first half of page 30, and in English it is -- this is page 81 of the English transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: "D.B.: Okay. Good morning. This is a recorded interview --"

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm just going to concentrate on the transcript. Do you see there you're now being asked questions and you're talking about a period at the end of July 1998 and beginning of August 1998 when there was the offensive, the Serb offensive? Do you see that's what the questions are about?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is the question about?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm just trying to direct your attention to this part of the transcript. Do you see that what's being talked about in this portion of the transcript is the Serb offensive at the end of July 1998 and the beginning of August 1998? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've given me the wrong page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Are you looking at page 29 and 30? The second half of page 29 and the first half of page 30. You're talking about the period from the beginning of August afterwards.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you remember, don't you, that the offensive, the Serb offensive, began for you in Zborce on the 25th and 26th of July, 1998? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the offensive occurred in Lapusnik at the same time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And by August the Serbs had moved all the way to Klecka. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the headquarters that was in Klecka had to move because the Serbs arrived. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And it moved to -- you think it moved to Divjake; right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I want to draw your attention to the middle of page 30 in the Albanian, and you see that -- you see you say you believe it moved to Divjake, that the headquarters moved to Divjake. And then the question is: "O.L.: Was Fatmir Limaj still in charge at that time?" And your answer is: "D.B.: "Yes." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my personal belief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what was that personal belief based on? Do you -- are you able to tell us?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, I thought that Fatmir Limaj was in Klecka. The commander of the point that was in Klecka, but not on the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So is the only mistake that you made in your interview, and you made it several times, is the only mistake that the -- that the headquarters in Klecka was in command of the area of the -- the area that you've marked in yellow in June and July of 1998? Was that the only mistake that you made in that interview?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't focus on the time. But I believe after the offensive this zone came under the Klecka command.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you joined the KLA in -- on April 20th of 1998, were you made aware of any rules in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rules were read to us and the oath we took.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What rules were read to you?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remembered three most important points. Maybe you have it here. I don't. Point 1, which we shouldn't misuse our uniforms for personal reasons. Then point 2 was that acts of revenge were forbidden. Point 3 was that any violation that was committed, the person should be held responsible. So we tried to abide by these rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And these rules were told to you when you joined the KLA?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Luan read these to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was there -- were there any -- did you learn of any rules, were you told any rules about the treatment of civilians?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was some. There were some rules. I don't remember them now, but we tried to abide by the orders and the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember when you heard about rules about the treatment of civilians?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Luan told me on the 20th of April about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And do you remember anything that he said about the treatment of civilians?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. If I were to read them, I would immediately recall them. I think they were international rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And why do you think they were international rules?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because every army has its own rules. So this army had an international rule too. I'm repeating Luan's words to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And those were words he said to you on the 20th of April or around there?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact date, but I do remember that it was Luan I heard those words from. Regarding the oath and the rules, that the KLA should abide by those, I heard on the 20th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And do you remember if the rules said something about you shouldn't abuse civilians or detain them or capture them? Did the rules say anything about that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Not exactly, but were they generally along those lines?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember that in June of 1998 the military police was -- there was military police present -- KLA military police present in Kroimire? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What month did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In June of 1998. Do you remember the military police being present?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not certain about the time they came to the Kroimire, when the military police was formed. I know there was military police, but I don't know the time, the exact time when they were formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: They were there sometime when Shukri Buja was there, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It was before the first -- before the Serb offensive at the end of July you saw military police in Kroimire, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I think a little while before the offensive there were some military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what was the job of the military police? What were their responsibilities?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had to take care of the soldiers, of the population. If there was an injustice done or when our members went to other points, in those cases they had to ask for some special permissions. So they checked on these permissions, these military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the military police, they would wear black uniforms?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did they've "PU" written on their uniforms, badges that said "PU"?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It is a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I raise one matter before the Court rises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Indeed Mr. Topolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: And it's as it were by way of an observation only. I don't understand the ruling the Court made regarding this witness as thereby giving the Prosecution blanket authority to lead. The question as to when the military police came into existence and in what circumstances is certainly, as far as my lay client is concerned, an engaged issue in these proceedings, and I wonder whether Mr. Whiting could reflect upon that when he has his coffee over the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The ruling of the Chamber was that there could be cross-examination on the past interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn until hopefully ten to six.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The witness -- Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, I want to draw your attention to the 14th of June, 1998. Do you remember that date?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when you were interviewed by the OTP you remembered that date as well, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What happened on that date?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were fightings in Carraleve.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where were you on that date?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the fightings, I was in Dug [as interpreted] to visit my daughter who was married there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you give the name of the village where you were again? It just -- I don't think the -- it was picked up clearly by the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dulje village above Petrastica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when did you learn that there was fighting in Carraleve?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard the shots and I ran to my positions, but when I went there, the fighting was over.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What time of day was this?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Midday, I think. I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And where -- can you describe for us where your positions were.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My positions were up to Zborce offensive. They were 25 metres as the crow flies from the main road, Stimlje-Prizren, in the middle of Carraleve.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I'm going to give you a piece of paper and ask that it be placed on the ELMO. And on that paper I'm going to ask, if you would, could you just draw the road that you just described, the Stimlje-Prizren road as it goes by Carraleve and the other roads that come off that road, the road that goes from that road in Carraleve to up to Petrastica. And then I'm going to ask you to draw where your positions were in relation to the road.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So on the left side you've written Dulje.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Shtime-Dulje-Prizren road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you've written on the first road coming from the direction of Shtime, the first road going right you've written --

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the road that least to Petrastica. This continues up to Komorane.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And where is Carraleve?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From here this is Carraleve, from this part to that part. And it extends even here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Even where? Can you mark where it extends?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I showed here the roads that were in the vicinity of my positions. I'm describing here the positions I held.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. First I'm going to ask -- we have to take this one step at a time so the record is clear. I'm going to ask that the record reflect that the witness when describing where Carraleve was, he put a line on the two ends of the road indicating that Carraleve is between those two lines. Now, Witness, what you've just drawn, the line with the two boxes, is that -- is that the position that you held in Carraleve at this time on the 14th of June?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could you just put a -- so the record is clear, could you just put a number 1 near what you've just drawn, that position.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And where is your house in relation to this diagram?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My house is approximately here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And could you put a number 2 next to what you've just drawn.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And are the Serb positions visible on this diagram that you've just drawn?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: On the 14th of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where the first tank was positioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could you put a number 3 next to that tank that you have drawn.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's where the tank was positioned on the 14th of June, 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In addition to that, there were three others closer -- a bit closer to me, that is to my positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And could you put a number 4 next to those three boxes which -- are those three boxes three tanks?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] Yes. There was also an armoured car and a tank at the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you draw where the mosque is?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where -- more or less where the mosque is. There was a tank and an armoured car stationed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could you put a number 5 there just so we have a clear record.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Is that mosque in Carraleve?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: These were the Serb positions on the 14th of June, 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were there on the 17th as well, in the same place.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us approximately what the distance is between your positions which you drew at number 1 and the closest Serb tanks which were at number 4? Can you tell us approximately what that distance is?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a hill from my position to the tank position. I saw only tank number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So you couldn't see tank number -- the three tanks at number 4? Those weren't visible to you?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were invisible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How did you know they were there?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came from Dulje, I saw the terrain. I saw what was there, and then I went to my position. On my way to my position, I saw the tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what is approximately -- the hill that you described, were your -- was your position on the hill?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tanks were in a valley, whereas I was higher up on the hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And can you tell us what approximately -- approximately the distances between your position and the tank you could see at position 3?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately 200 metres away as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the tank and armoured car that was at position 5 at the mosque, was that visible to you at your position at 1, number 1? Could you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, these tanks and the armoured car, were they VJ or MUP, if you know?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tank was VJ. The armoured car belonged to the MUP, M-U-P.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So you have identified five tanks. Those five tanks were all VJ tanks?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were others, but they were further away from our positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In which direction?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the direction of Shtime. But there were also some others at Dulje pass.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And your testimony is that you were -- you held -- you were at position 1 after the filing on the 14th of June and then again during the fighting on the 17th of June; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that this drawing be given a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will be Prosecution Exhibit P118.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And while I'm at it so I don't forget, I'll also ask that the map that was referred to earlier, U003-3748, be given a number as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The map will be given Prosecution Exhibit number P119.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that there was more fighting on the 17th of June, 1998. Is that a date that you remembered in your interview with the OTP?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened on that date.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On 17th of June, a friend of ours came and informed us that the Serb forces had entered Carraleve, military and police forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where were you when you learned that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Petrastica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And do you remember who the friend was who informed you of this?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A friend of mine whom I had appointed to reconnoitre the ground from Carraleve to see where the Serb forces were heading. He was cooperating with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what's his name?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Majrush [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could you say it again? I don't think the interpreter could hear.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bajrush.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And his last name?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hafa [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what did he tell you in Petrastica?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that police and military forces have entered Carraleve. Immediately I informed the soldiers and told them to take up positions. We had to meet with other soldiers from Kroimire and with Luan. From there we took new tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did Luan -- was Luan there when Bajrush came and gave you this information?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was not there. He was in Kroimire. I was in Petrastica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you inform Luan in Kroimire what you had learned?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did he tell you to go to Carraleve to your position?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had agreed that I sent a soldier to inform Luan, and then I went to the meeting place. This meeting place was supposed to be on a hill in Carraleve.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what happened at the meeting place? Did Luan come?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as I went there, Luan came too. Both of us had soldiers with us, and we were given new tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Luan gave you the tasks?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With six soldiers, I went -- I had to leave two at the neighbourhood road, and four I had to take with me at the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And this is the position that you drew for us on the diagram?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you describe this position for the Court? What was it?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two bunkers there. Usually I stayed there with three soldiers, that is four of us, for a long time, as of 19 June until the Zborce offensive. I protected my family and the neighbourhood, which was a bit far from our position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said there were two bunkers there. Were there also trenches?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How many trenches were there?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four and two bunkers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How long were the trenches, how many metres?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My position was some 100 metres. You can see them today. They are still there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the bunkers, what were they made out of?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bunkers were made out of very solid wood, gravel, all these things to make it strong.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were the bunkers at the ends of -- at one end of the trenches or in the middle of the trenches or ...

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second bunker was at the end of the trench, the first. The second one was in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What happened after you got to your position?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there. I was alone even though it was very difficult to pass through the road up to my position. I told my friend who were behind me, "If they attack me, you shouldn't join the battle." So I went that way. They attacked me. The soldiers didn't follow me, as I said, so I was alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what happened? Did you have -- before you answer that question, did you have a weapon? Did you have a gun?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I never went there without a gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what happened? You were alone at the position. What happened?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fighting broke out even though the positions -- there were three positions. There was one in front of me and one on the left side of the road. There were other soldiers of ours stationed there. So the fighting broke out. I started to fight too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The three positions, were they all located at the place that you indicated on the diagram marked with a number 1?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were others. I marked only my position in that diagram.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And can you describe for us where the other positions were in relation to your position?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to draw them?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Actually, if the exhibit could be put back in front of the witness. I believe it's P118. Yes. Great. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm putting number 2 here in the second position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If the record could reflect that where the witness has drawn a second position he's marked a P.2 and put a circle around it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the third position, sir, where was that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where it was, across my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if the record could reflect that the witness has drawn a line and put a P followed by a 3 where the third position was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And just before we take away this diagram, were you -- at number 1, your position, you were alone at that position?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But the -- but your testimony was there were other soldiers, other KLA soldiers at position 2 and position 3?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And this is on the 17th of June?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the 17th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You can take away the diagram. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, you testified that the fighting broke out. What happened next?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After three hours of fighting, I was injured in the position I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I believe you testified yesterday that the injury was on your arm, on your right arm or shoulder; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On my right arm here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What did you do after you were injured?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I resisted for who have an hour there as the fighting went on. Then when the Serb forces withdrew --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I returned to the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You returned --

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I went home, which was close to my position. I tied my wounds, and then I went to the place where I met Luan and the other soldiers usually. There were many civilians there. They had heard the firing, the fire shots, so they took me in a car and took me to a doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where was the doctor that they took you to?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Shale.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were you treated by a doctor in Shale?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He cleaned the wounds, and he told me to go to Gajrak.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Before you went to Gajrak, did you -- what was in Gajrak?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a doctor who usually treated the wounds. Until that moment, I didn't know anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Before you went to Gajrak, did you go back to Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you see somebody in Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met Fatmir Limaj. Haxhi Shala was there, and some other war comrades.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Is this still on the 17th of June?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And why did you think Fatmir Limaj and Haxhi Shala were in Kroimire on that day?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't know why they were there. For me it matters that they were war comrades. I didn't know why they were there, where they were going.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you think that they were there because of the fighting?

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Well, I do, I really do. He's given an answer, he doesn't know. I don't think there should be a licence to ask anything you want despite the answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It was a question that is not within the bounds of ordinary questioning, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If I could just have a moment, Your Honour. I'll move on. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you know Fatmir Limaj's name on that date? Did you know him as Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I knew him as Celiku. It was later that I found out that his name was Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When did you find out later that his name was Fatmir Limaj?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember if it was in 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember if it was during the war or was it after the war?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe -- maybe during the war, but it must have been after the offensive or by the end of the war. I am not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But in any event, on the 17th of June, you knew him as Celiku. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And Haxhi Shala, did you know him as Haxhi Shala on that date or did you know him by another name?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As Topi [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, did you go from somewhere to Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Kroimire we went to Klecka. There Topi sent me to Gajrak to be treated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, who went to Klecka?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went. They sent me, Mr. Fatmir, Celiku. Shala was there, Haxhi Shala. As far as I remember, Guri was there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know Guri's real name?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't get his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could you repeat? The translator could not hear what you said. Guri's real name.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jetu [phoen] Jashari.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How did you get to Klecka from Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I will. How did you get from Kroimire to Klecka?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went there by a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And who was in the car?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fatmir Limaj, I said earlier, Haxhi Shala, and Jetu Jashari plus the driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know who the driver was?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And in Klecka -- from Klecka where did you go?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After Klecka, Topi sent me to the doctor in Gajrak.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did you go to Gajrak?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did you go alone?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With Haxhi Shala, aka Topi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, on the way from -- so Fatmir Limaj stayed in Klecka?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: During the drive from Kroimire to Klecka, did you have any conversation with Fatmir Limaj, or Celiku as you knew him?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We talked.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What did you talk about?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me about the situation in Carraleve, how things were going there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what did you tell him?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told him that the Serb police are coming there for five times a day along the main road, which I could see from my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what did he say?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that we don't have any orders to fight, and we discussed this issue together. Then he told me when this is the case, you don't have to wait for orders by someone. You can act.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did he tell you what -- what that meant, you can act? You can act, did he explain what he meant by that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was an informal talk, so don't wait for orders. Whether they are police or soldiers, you don't have to wait for orders but do what you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And just to make it clear to the Court, did he say what he meant by "do what you can" when there was Serb police or soldiers? What was he saying you should do?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wanted to tell me that if you have a good position, you can attack them, and you may attack them. You don't have to wait for orders to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, after you went -- when you arrived in Gajrak, was that still on the 17th of June?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the evening. Maybe it was midnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were you treated there by a doctor?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He treated my wound. He cleaned it, and he bandaged it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Gajrak?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until he treated my wound, and then we returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember how long that was?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Half an hour or one hour at the most. It was a small place. There were other wounded people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember how many other wounded people were there?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the room where I was, there were two injured people. One was from Blac. He was wounded by a sniper, shot at him in Dulje pass. A Serb sniper had shot him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And was there just one doctor at this place in Gajrak or was there more than one?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was one doctor that took care of me. I don't know about the others. It didn't see. It was midnight, I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: After you spent -- after you were treated in Gajrak, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Luznica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how long did you stay in Luznica?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That night, I think it was the 18th or the 19th, that I returned to Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was there a point in Luznica?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the point in Luznica, if you knew?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ismet Jashari was the commander of that point, aka Kumanova.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you know him as Ismet Jashari or as Kumanova at that time?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As Kumanova.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You returned, I think you said, to Petrastica. Do you remember what date you got back to Petrastica?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, it was 19th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And during your interview with the OTP, did -- you remembered that date as well, didn't you? I see you nodded, but for the record you have to give an answer.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you. When you returned to Petrastica, did you -- was there a change in the number of soldiers that you saw there?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The number had increased. It was over 50 or 60 soldiers who had come from different places. They had joined us at the point where we were positioned. So when I received a new task, I took three soldiers and went to my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where did the soldiers -- these 50 or 60 soldiers come from, what different places?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Nekovce, Bajice, Shale. They had all gathered in Petrastica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did any soldiers come from Lapusnik?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the attack on the 17th of June, after I was wounded, I went to the place where I met Luan. And that's where I saw Shala and Voglushi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Who did you -- who did you see when you -- I'm just going to ask you to repeat the answer. Who did you see when you -- when you went to the place where you met with Luan after you were injured?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I was wounded, on the way to the second or third positions that they held, I saw that Ymer Alushani, aka Voglushi, was on those positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That was unclear in the translation there. So you saw Yme3r, known as Voglushi. Was that the first time you had seen this person?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I knew this person from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: From when?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him from 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when you saw him on the 17th of June, 1998, was that the first time you had seen him since you had joined the KLA on the 20th of April, 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'd seen him several times but not on our positions but as a reinforcement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where had you seen him?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, he was in Petrastica several times. His uncles lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And he came as reinforcement? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since he was on his second positions, on our positions, I believed he came there to assist us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And where did he come from? What -- when he came to Petrastica, what village was he coming from?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He comes from Komorane. He was from Komorane. I knew he was from Komorane.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But did you -- when he wasn't in Petrastica, do you know what village he was in?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know where he was active. Later on, I found out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What did you find out later on?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found out that he was in Lapusnik, a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when you -- when you saw him on the 17th of June and several times before that in Petrastica, how did you know him, as Ymer Alushani or as Voglushi?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As Ymer Alushani. I as I said, I knew him from 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you learn his pseudonym -- or let me put this this way: When did you hear the name Voglushi?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You think it was during this time in June of 1998 that you heard that name?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. To tell you the truth, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, you said that you -- on the 17th of June, you saw him at the -- after you were injured at the place where you met with Luan. Where was that exactly?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the location where we would meet to receive new tasks. That's where I met Ymer Alushani.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And my question was what village was that location in?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was between the villages of Carraleve and Pjetershtice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what kind of place was it? Was it a building? Was it a house? Was it a ...

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a road, Carraleve-Komorane road, and then there was another junction that was going to Zborce. This is the cemetery, the location where the cemetery of our village was located. That's where we would meet. There was no house. It was the top of a hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So the meeting point was out in the open. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a meadow. There was no features there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When Ymer Alushani came to Petrastica and Carraleve, did he -- do you know if he came with others, with other soldiers that were with him?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wounded. I know that Ymer came out. He greeted me. He asked me about the situation. I told him that the Serb forces had withdrawn. There was nobody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the times that you spoke about before this date, before the 17th of June when you came to Petrastica, did he come with others or did he come alone?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what time you are referring to for the moment. Is it before or after the 17th?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I believe you testified that he had come several times before the 17th of June to Petrastica. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about that day. The fact is I've seen him several times in Pjetershtice. I have seen him leave for Rance is several times as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And those several times was he alone or with other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With Commander Qerqizi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember when was the first time you saw Commander Qerqizi with Ymer Alushani?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that date, but to my knowledge it was sometime in June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did you know Qerqiz's real name?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on, I learned his real name, sometime by the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what did you learn his real name to be?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the end of the war, I found out that he was Isak Musliu and he was from Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How many times did you see Ymer Alushani and Isak Musliu, Qerqiz, in Petrastica in June of 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two types. They passed by on their way to Rance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did you hear anything about what Commander Qerqiz was doing in Rance?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he was going to establish a point there as well, a KLA point.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did you believe that in -- this was in June of 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I believe, yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: By the way, Ymer Alushani, Voglushi, did you hear at some point about -- that he was killed?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during the offensive in July.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you hear where he was killed?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the July offensive at Zborce, the -- on the same day the Lapusnik offensive took place, and two days later I heard that Ymer Alushani was killed at Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, after you returned to Petrastica, Carraleve on the 19th of June, 1998, was there any fighting after that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was fighting on the 23rd of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And where did that fighting occur?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the same positions. I was with three other soldiers. We were, altogether, four.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And do you know if there was -- if there were soldiers in the other positions, positions 2 and 3?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how long did the fighting last?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. Maybe two to three hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what happened as a result of the fighting?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was anticipating the moment. Since I didn't have anti-tank weapons, I used bottles with petrol.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What did you do with those bottles?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We attacked the three last tanks. Twenty-five bottles with petrol.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what happened?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was severe fighting because they would shoot usually at withdrawal, not on frontal combat. So as they were withdrawing with the tanks, there was fighting going on until the turn. When they turned that, I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were any of the tanks damaged?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did the tanks withdraw?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was throwing the bottles, and I couldn't notice because there was uninterrupted fire. I was on a combat position, and I was just throwing the bottles.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: After that date was there more fighting with the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly. There were not great fightings. Mainly they would come and attack. I will just single out the fact that more than 100 tanks attacked our positions. Forty tanks were on the Dulje pass and about 60 at Shtime.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when did that occur?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened, if I'm not mistaken here, on the 25th of July. They were attacking from both sides, and at one occasion, it was on the 25th, a shell fell and one was killed and -- and one was wounded and two were killed. I was informed by position number 3 that there was a wounded person at the mosque. I placed myself in danger, took the car and picked up the wounded person to -- brought him to Petrastica. He had his left arm and his leg wounded. His leg was badly wounded, almost cut off. I'm glad to hear that he was treated later on in Italy and that he is now in a good state.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And where did you go after you took this person to Petrastica?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took him to Petrastica. I said to them, "Do the best you can. Send him somewhere else," and I returned myself to my position. The person who was wounded had also his brother and his father killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how long did you stay at your position? This is on the 25th of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed at my position non-stop that day and that night. It was a mistake. It was -- I said 25th, but it was the 24th. On the 25th was the Zborce offensive. This is in July. And this young man, he was wounded in June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. So that was which date in June? Which battle in June, the 14th, the 17th, or the 23rd?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 25th of June. It was on this date that I took this young man, wounded young man. It was 25th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the offensive, the Zborce offensive, started on the 25th of July?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And was that when there were a hundred tanks?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were surrounded by 100 tanks approximately, while at Zborce there were about 60 armoured vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And where were you? Were you in your position or somewhere else on the 25th of July?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at my positions on the 25th of July. On the 26th of July, Luan came and told me to withdraw from there because there was nothing going on there because the Serb forces would not pass by there. So I went opposite to the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Is that the mosque in Carraleve that you drew on the diagram?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what happened there?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We constructed a barricade so as to prevent the Serb population from preventing into the population and the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Till the 27th, to my knowledge. Till the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How many soldiers were you with at that position?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was with the same soldiers who were with me in my positions, and there were several others a little bit above the location where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And were you successful in preventing the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They stopped at Zborce, and they didn't penetrate any deeper.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And then where did you go? On the 17th, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received the order to withdraw and to return to the last positions we held.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did you go back to -- is that you went back to your position in Carraleve then?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At the positions between Petrastica and Carraleve.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Till the next day. And then we went back to the point in Petrastica, to the house where we were earlier, because from 23rd of June, the main road Shtime-Dulje-Prizren was not passable.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And after you went back to the house in Petrastica, how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stayed there, and we operated until the August offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember when in August that offensive occurred?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be more precise, I have something here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Could you tell -- tell us, please, what it is you're looking at.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm looking at the date. It's on the 27th of August when the offensive at Zborce took place. And then from Zborce it passed to Petrastica and then to the area on this side.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Before you answered that question you opened up something at your table and looked at a paper. Can you just tell us what it is that you looked at?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an exact date. This is something where I keep some important dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Would you mind if -- could I see that paper, please?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if this is a convenient time for the break, and perhaps if I could just ask the witness if I could keep this piece of paper overnight until tomorrow's session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I have course I will share this with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're going to have to adjourn again. It's reached the hour when we must stop. We will resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 2nd day of February 2005, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.58 p.m.,
